adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens()` which, in sync mode, returns the raw `fetch()` `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:7-18). Multiple migrated callers still assume their original non-fetch response shapes: Google Calendar now does `const token = res?.data` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~83-90), which will be `undefined` on a `Response`. Hubspot assigns the return value to `HubspotToken` (packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:~174-191), but in sync mode it would be a `Response`, so subsequent property reads (e.g., `expiresIn`) would fail. Additionally, some services (e.g., Webex) still parse the provider-specific token response via their existing handlers, but sync mode’s comment says the endpoint "should only contain the access token and expiry date" (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:9-10), which would not satisfy those handlers’ expected fields. This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior break when sync mode is enabled.
